You are being evaluated on Continual-ARC, a lifelong stream of ARC-style grid puzzles.
Each puzzle instance has a task id and a test input grid. Tasks recur across the
stream with fresh inputs. Each instance is a separate conversation: the next one
starts without this one's messages.

On every message you must choose exactly one action and put it as a JSON object
on the last line of your reply:
  {"action": "submit", "grid": [[0, 1, 2], [3, 4, 5]]}   submit an output grid
  {"action": "request_demos"}                            ask for one more demonstration pair for this task
  {"action": "finish"}                                   end the instance, once it is over
Grids are lists of rows; cells are integers 0-9; dimensions are 1-30.

Each demo request returns one more input-output pair of the task, up to the demo cap shown
with the input.

Scoring: an instance you solve costs 1 for each wrong submission and 1 for
each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until
the instance is over. Each instance is scored on its own, and lower cost is better.

'For ARC task-3375ff3f (repeated noisy-rectangle task), reconstruct every solid axis-aligned rectangular color block and remove isolated noise. The grid background is usually the dominant color; real blocks can be multiple different colors (including 0), and can be as small as 2x2. A rectangle may contain isolated cells of arbitrary noise colors or background-colored holes; fill its full bounding rectangle with the block color. Set all unrelated/noise cells outside rectangles to background. Do not assume only one foreground color, and do not require a block to be large. Carefully inspect every row when finding each rectangle’s full extent: this test had a large 8 block extending through row 10 while another 8 rectangle began at row 10 in separate columns; omitting that one row caused incorrect submissions.

Accepted task test, 0-indexed geometry (background 2): 8 blocks r0-1 c0-1; r1-3 c12-14; r4-10 c1-7; r6-8 c12-17; r10-14 c9-14; r12-13 c18-19. 9 blocks r0-2 c6-7; r0-1 c18-19; r3-4 c9-10; r13-14 c3-5. Fill those rectangles, set all other cells to 2. Corruptions inside blocks included 0/1/5/6, and isolated noise included 5 at r7c10, 0 at r10c18 and r11c0. Note r14c5=0 was a corruption inside the 9 block.

Demos also establish that small 2x2 blocks are legitimate (demo 4, color 7 at r7-8 c0-1); do not discard them merely for small area. Demo patterns showed several different block colors in one grid and isolated stray singletons of other colors should be reset. Previously summarized accepted example: background 0, 8 rectangles r2-5 c2-6, r3-6 c9-12, r8-9 c7-13; 1 rectangles r0-6 c14-16, r1-2 c22-27, r4-9 c18-23, r4-8 c25-29, r7-11 c2-5. All coordinates 0-indexed, bounding rectangles inclusive.

Accepted task test 2 (background 3): blocks were 4 rectangles r0-4 c0-2; r2-7 c5-8; r10-16 c4-6; 1 rectangle r1-6 c10-11; 5 rectangle r9-11 c8-9; 8 rectangle r13-18 c10-11. Isolated noise colors 2/9 were restored to the block color when within a rectangle, otherwise to background 3. Example: r0c1=2 was inside the 4 rectangle and became 4; r0c3=2 was outside and became 3. Use the bounding boxes of same-color solid rectangles to classify noise; multiple blocks can have same color, and their row spans may touch/overlap while columns remain separate.

Accepted test example (background 2, 13x15): output consists of three solid 6 rectangles: rows 1-4, cols 5-7; rows 3-4, cols 9-12; rows 6-10, cols 5-10 (0-indexed, inclusive). All other cells are 2. Input included isolated noise outside blocks and corruptions within these rectangles (e.g. 7, 3, 8, 4, 0); fill the rectangles with 6 and reset outside noise to background.

Additional accepted test (18x24, background 2): restore five rectangles of color 5 at r0-6 c8-11, r8-14 c4-7, r10-11 c9-13, and r9-11 c17-19, plus two color-9 rectangles at r3-6 c17-18 and r14-17 c11-16 (0-indexed inclusive). Fill all rectangle cells, including corrupted cells/holes (noise colors 0,1,3,4,6,8); set all other noise cells to 2. This confirms arbitrary noise colors are handled by location: within rectangle => rectangle color, outside => background.

Additional accepted test (26x29, background 1): restore a 3x3 color-7 rectangle at rows 2-4, cols 9-11 (it had a 0 at r2c10); a 3x6 color-3 rectangle at rows 21-23, cols 10-15 (it had a 0 at r22c14); and a 2x3 color-5 rectangle at rows 22-23, cols 3-5. Set all isolated noise cells to background 1, including the 8 adjacent to the 5 block. Submitted correctly after filling the two rectangle anomalies with their block colors. This supports locating blocks from the complete rectangle pattern and classifying speckles by whether they lie inside or outside a block.

Additional accepted test (18x23, background 6): restore color-3 rectangle r0-4 c3-7; color-7 rectangles r2-6 c14-19, r10-11 c4-9, and r11-12 c18-19; color-2 rectangle r15-16 c7-13 (0-indexed, inclusive). Reset all other cells, including isolated colors 1/4/5/8/9, to 6. Noise examples: r5c3 and r5c6=4, r11c6=8 inside the color-7 r10-11/c4-9 rectangle, r11c17=8 adjacent to but outside the 2x2 color-7 block, and r6c20=5. Correct output was accepted. This further confirms 2x2 rectangles are valid and noises are classified by bounding-box inclusion.

Accepted test (29x13, background 8): restore color-7 rectangles at rows 0-4, cols 4-9 and rows 9-15, cols 10-12, plus a color-4 rectangle at rows 25-27, cols 8-12 (all zero-indexed, inclusive). Fill all rectangle cells uniformly and set every other cell to background 8. Input corruptions inside blocks included (0,5)=5, (1,7)=3, (2,9)=2, (4,6)=2; (15,11)=2 inside the second 7 block; and (27,11)=3 inside the 4 block. All scattered 2/3/5/9 cells outside these boxes, including around rows 5-24 and (28,8), were noise and restored to 8. This test was accepted with no wrong submissions.'
